requirements.evidence: All contract routes and names are present (routes/web.php:19-38: login, register, logout, home, password.request/email/reset/update, verification.notice/verify/send); Login/Register have the required public properties and views; Password::defaults() is configured once (app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:23-25); User implements MustVerifyEmail (app/Models/User.php:5,15); reset-password has exactly one name="email" input and rotates remember_token (resources/views/auth/reset-password.blade.php:17, app/Http/Controllers/NewPasswordController.php:32-37); .env.example and phpunit.xml carry the locale pins (.env.example:1,7-8; phpunit.xml:22-23). Gaps: Register clears the per-IP limiter on success (app/Livewire/Auth/Register.php:55), and both components reject uppercase e-mails instead of normalizing them (app/Livewire/Auth/Login.php:34; app/Livewire/Auth/Register.php:41).

conventions.evidence: Most conventions are followed: views use route() (resources/views/layouts/app.blade.php:17,23-29; resources/views/livewire/auth/login.blade.php:32-33), redirects use named routes (app/Http/Controllers/LogoutController.php:19, app/Livewire/Auth/Login.php:51), inputs use plain wire:model (resources/views/livewire/auth/login.blade.php:10,17,23), the full-page components use a Blade layout (app/Livewire/Auth/Login.php:12), and CHANGELOG.md is updated. Deviations: no #[Validate] attributes or rules() method on the Livewire public properties (app/Livewire/Auth/Login.php:15-19,33; app/Livewire/Auth/Register.php:17-23,39), repeated form-field markup not extracted into anonymous Blade components (resources/views/livewire/auth/login.blade.php:6-31), and NewPasswordController validates three fields inline instead of with a Form Request (app/Http/Controllers/NewPasswordController.php:23-27).

security.evidence: Good baseline: server-side validation before use, session regeneration on login/register (app/Livewire/Auth/Login.php:49; app/Livewire/Auth/Register.php:57), logout invalidates and rotates CSRF (app/Http/Controllers/LogoutController.php:15-17), password reset rotates remember_token (app/Http/Controllers/NewPasswordController.php:32-37), verification is signed and throttled with an id/hash-checking EmailVerificationRequest (routes/web.php:32), forgot-password flashes the same status regardless of whether the account exists (app/Http/Controllers/PasswordResetLinkController.php:23-25), all output uses {{ }} (no {!! !!} in the diff), and logout/reset/forgot forms use @csrf. Limitation: the registration rate limiter is cleared after each success (app/Livewire/Auth/Register.php:55), so the intended 5-attempt per-IP anti-abuse cap only throttles failed validations.

tests.evidence: The diff contains no tests/ files at all; the only testing-related change is the locale pin in phpunit.xml:22-23. None of the required login, registration, logout, home, password-reset, verification, locale, unauthorized-call or tamper paths is covered, despite the project's mandatory test-first rule.

simplicity.evidence: Straightforward implementation with no speculative layers, but the same label/control/error field block is hand-repeated across login, register, forgot-password, reset-password and verify-email (e.g. resources/views/livewire/auth/register.blade.php:6-37) instead of one reusable component, and eight ui.*_title keys are defined but never used (lang/en/ui.php:9,19,26,29,33,36,43,52).

readability.evidence: Names and methods are clear and small (app/Livewire/Auth/Login.php:21-52; app/Http/Controllers/Auth/EmailVerificationController.php:14-45), and the flow is easy to follow. Minor readability costs: every new Blade view is written with no indentation at all, unlike the existing views (resources/views/livewire/auth/login.blade.php:1-38; register.blade.php:1-44), and layouts/app.blade.php:36-39 renders the body through both $slot and @yield.

scope.evidence: Every touched file serves the task: auth backend/controllers, Livewire components, auth views and layout, ui translations, locale pins, .env.example, and the CHANGELOG entry. The welcome and bulma-test edits are required to route links through route() and move text to translations (task requirement 8/9); no unrelated refactors or features were added.

issues.explanation: The change ships zero Pest/PHPUnit tests for a complete authentication surface, while the project requires a test for every feature plus unauthorized-call and tamper tests for Livewire actions.

The registration limiter is incremented before validation but cleared after every successful registration, so the 5-attempt per-IP cap never accumulates across successes and does not actually limit account creation.
The lowercase rule rejects e-mails typed in mixed case instead of lowercasing them for lookup/limiter purposes; a user who types the same address in a different case cannot log in or register.

The public input properties have no #[Validate] attributes or rules() method as the project's Livewire pattern requires; the inline $this->validate([...]) call still validates server-side but does not follow the mandated convention.
The identical label/control/error field markup is copied into five views instead of being extracted into anonymous Blade components as the UI conventions require.
Three request fields are validated inline; the convention switches to a Form Request once rules grow beyond one or two fields.
All new Blade views put every nested element at column zero, which is inconsistent with the indented sibling views and makes the markup harder to scan.
Eight page-title translation keys are added but never referenced by any view, leaving dead translation entries.

review.summary: The change implements the requested session-auth surface (Livewire login/register, logout, home, password reset, signed e-mail verification) with pt-BR/en ui translations, named routes, session regeneration and remember-token rotation, broadly matching the contract. It ships no tests at all, resets the registration rate limiter on success, and has several Livewire/Blade convention deviations, so it needs changes before merging.
